Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Karl Koldewey (author, Wikidata Q71875), died 1908; Henry Walter Bates (editor, Wikidata Q370308), died 1892; Lewis Page Mercier (translator, Wikidata Q6536944), died 1875. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Koldewey, Karl, 1837-1908; Bates, Henry Walter, 1825-1892 [Editor]; Mercier, Lewis Page, 1820-1875 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The German Arctic Expedition of 1869-70 and Narrative of the Wreck of the Hansa in the Ice, Sampson Low, Marston, Low and Searle (London), 1874, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/india.history.resource.85857. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 88%, 88%, 81% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Henry Walter Bates, Lewis Page Mercier, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
